It is time for the weekly update again. Last week's came out well, after you told the AI exactly what to include, what to skip and how to order it. What did you type?

## Why it is hard

Good instructions get lost. They sit in an old conversation or in your head, so each time you rebuild them from memory and the result is a little different. A step gets forgotten: the blocked work, the dates, the thing your lead always asks about.

And when a teammate does the same job, they start from nothing and do it their own way.

## How Genos helps

A **skill** is a note of written steps with a name. Write it once, in plain words, as you would brief a colleague. Then type `/` at the start of a question and pick it.

```flow
Write the steps once
Type / and pick it
Read the result
Approve any change
```

A skill can only read, or it can also propose changes. If it proposes one, you still see it and approve it before anything happens.

Some examples of steps worth keeping:

- the weekly update: what closed, what is stuck, what is next
- a meeting follow-up: turn the notes into actions with owners
- a risk check before a deadline

## What you get

- **The same instructions every time**, without remembering the wording.
- **Less setup.** The steps are already there; you add only what is different today, such as a project name.
- **A shared way of doing it.** Share a skill with your team or with chosen people; they install it and run the version you published. Fix a step and publish again; people who installed it are told, and take the update when they choose.
- **Runs on a schedule.** A schedule can run your skill at set times and put the result in your Inbox. A scheduled run only reads; it changes nothing.

Running a skill is asking Genos, so it uses your AI allowance. Proposing changes needs Core or above, and so do schedules.

## How to start

1. Open **Settings → Genos → Skills**. Start from a template or a blank skill.
2. Write the steps you would give a new teammate. Give it a short name.
3. In the ask box (Cmd-K, or Ctrl-K), type `/` and choose it.

Pick the thing you explained twice this week. That is your first skill.
